- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term momentum.
- After sharp price spikes in history, model overreacts with exaggerated upward forecasts (overshoot), then corrects too late.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after peaks.
- Forecasts often underestimate the magnitude of late-period price increases (last 5–10 days of 30d), especially when true outcomes show strong upward momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 10–20), while true outcomes often show upward correction or stabilization.
- When history shows strong downward trend, model fails to anticipate the reversal — underestimates rebound potential.
- Model tends to ignore recent volatility in history, leading to overly smooth forecasts that miss sharp reversals or spikes.
